svg.title: Measuring a spring’s force constant
svg.desc: (a) A graph of the restoring force F, equal to the weight supported, versus the displacement x of a spring, for masses of 0 to 0.500 kg: weights 0, 0.98, 1.96, 2.94, 3.92 and 4.90 N give displacements 0, 0.025, 0.050, 0.076, 0.099 and 0.127 m. The points lie on a straight line through the origin, so the spring obeys Hooke’s law; the slope, rise over run, is the force constant k, about 39 N/m. (b) The same data table, and a spring hanging from a support, unstretched at x = 0 and stretched to x1 and x2 by masses m1 and m2 whose weights are w1 and w2.
